title: Residents voice concerns over conditions at Daviess County Animal Shelter - NewsBreak
text:
By Andrew Newland Ann Powell ,
1 hours ago
DAVIESS COUNTY, Ky. (WEHT) -- Concern is growing among animal activists over the treatment of animals in the Daviess County Animal Shelter.
Residents say the concern started a few months after It Takes a Village took over the shelter last April. Julia Campbell lives in Daviess County and says it feels like concerns are falling on deaf ears.
“I am not going to accuse anyone of anything, but I'm going to say I have some legitimate concerns,” Campbell said. “And if this isn't the time for our fiscal court to really question themselves, was this the right choice?”
It Takes a Village disagrees. Shelter officials say staff have never been asked to reduce costs by withholding or limiting food from the animals in our care. They say any claim suggesting otherwise is false and add animals can experience weight loss due to stress.
Wayne Mcelvain says the pictures and actions speak for themselves. He says the desire to volunteer is going downhill.
“All of these people are taxpayers that want to volunteer and do things. And they, you know, you have to sign an NDA to volunteer and walk a dog is ridiculous. You know what I mean
Campbell and Mcelvain both say it's an issue with policy and follow through. Although they say the shelter's heart is in the right place, the agency is in over its head and is putting animals at risk.
“If you have become overwhelmed, please bow out and allow the shelter to return so that Daviess County citizens can have once again say over something we are all so very passionate about,” Campbell said.
